canonical_question: Why was 40 hours selected as the critical milling time to achieve homogeneity instead of 30 or 50 hours?

question_variants.question: Why was 40 hours selected as the critical milling time to achieve homogeneity instead of 30 or 50 hours?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper states that 40 hours was the milling time prolonged to obtain alloy powders with homogeneous composition. It does not provide a comparative analysis or data explaining why 30 or 50 hours were not selected as the critical time.

answers.answer: The milling time is prolonged to 40 h in order to obtain alloy powders with homogeneous composition. The paper notes intermittent sampling at 5, 10, 20, 30, and 40 h, but does not explicitly state the specific reason why 40 h was chosen over 30 or 50 h other than achieving homogeneity.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative data for 30 vs 40 vs 50 hours provided to justify the specific choice
evidence_spans: Figure 1 a shows the XRD patterns of the equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi high entropy alloy powders with different milling times.
Subsequently, two overlapping peaks near the peaks of W and Mo, characterized as body-centered cubic (BCC) solutions, are observed in the XRD pattern after 20 h.

It can be hypothesized that the solid solution sequence of the elements is related to the melting point, with low-melting-point elements being dissolved more quickly than the elements with higher melting points, which has been similarly reported in the previous work [ [18] ].
